lessons.title: Support without biting
lessons.goal: Hold a written B4 with comfortable jaw and steady air.
steps: Adjust the neck strap so the mouthpiece meets you without leaning the head forward; rest the right thumb rather than carrying the sax by the jaw.
Play B4 for four counts then rest four, keeping corners supportive without squeezing the reed shut.
Compare the start and end of the tone; if dizzy, uncomfortable or breathless, stop and return to normal breathing before continuing.
lessons.pattern: Written B4(4), rest(4), B4(4), rest(4); concert D4
quiz: Steady comfortable air, not excessive biting
Lifting the sax with the mouth

lessons.title: Read written B in treble clef
lessons.goal: Locate B4 on the middle treble line.
steps: Treble lines bottom-up are E4-G4-B4-D5-F5; B4 sits on the middle line.
Draw five lines, mark B4, and point to each repeated note before sounding it.
Play four B quarter notes, distinguishing written B from the concert D shown by the tuner; those are not conflicting measurements.
lessons.pattern: Four written B4 quarters; treble middle line; concert D4

lessons.title: Written pitch and sounding pitch
lessons.goal: Hear the concert D reference for a written alto B.
steps: Hear the app's reference for written B4; it produces concert D4 because alto sax sounds nine semitones lower.
Play B fingering and compare the sound, using small steady-air adjustments rather than biting to force agreement.
Play, release, and repeat; one held tone produces one pitch hit, not repeated score. Hum the concert reference in a comfortable octave.
lessons.pattern: Written B4 -> concert D4; repeat with releases

lessons.title: Count attacks and breathing rests
lessons.goal: Keep the count through a planned breath.
steps: Count four B4 quarter notes at40 BPM with a gentle tongue release for each attack.
Next bar stays silent for four beats while you take an easy breath.
Repeat without shortening the rest bar; breathing space is written musical time, not an unmeasured pause.
lessons.pattern: | B B B B | rest(4) |; quarters then measured breathing bar
quiz: Retain the pulse and bar length
Be skipped if you have air

lessons.title: Original melody: Single Breeze
lessons.goal: Shape a repeated-note phrase with a complete release.
steps: Play written | B(1) B(1) B(2) | then rest for one full bar.
Make the third B slightly softer while holding two beats; keep pitch steady as air decreases.
Give two takes with quiet releases and normal breathing between them. Judge tone quality by listening in addition to tuner feedback.
lessons.pattern: | B4 B4 B4(2) | rest(4) |; written pitch

lessons.title: Stay close to the pearls
lessons.goal: Change B-A-G without high finger lifts.
steps: Written B uses left index, A adds left middle, G adds left ring. Keep fingers curved naturally over the pearls.
Move silently B-A-G-A-B, watching fingers remain close instead of springing away.
Sound the pattern with one relaxed air stream, then tongue each note; rest if you press keys hard enough to tense the wrist.
lessons.pattern: Written B4 A4 G4 A4 B4; close fingers, light key pressure

lessons.title: Read the three-note contour
lessons.goal: Read G4, A4 and B4 by staff position.
steps: G4 is the second treble line, A4 the space above it, B4 the middle line.
Draw G-A-B-A-G and say whether each move rises or falls before playing.
Cover labels and read by adjacent positions; the treble guide is written pitch, while tuner names concert pitch.
lessons.pattern: G4 A4 B4 A4 G4; adjacent treble positions
quiz: Between the G4 and B4 lines

lessons.title: Three notes inside G major
lessons.goal: Hear G as home in a G-A-B fragment.
steps: Play G4-A4-B4 ascending, then descend to G.
Sing degrees1-2-3 in concert pitch if possible; use a comfortable octave rather than trying to sing written labels at sax transposition.
Create an answer B-A-G held for two beats, breathing only after the phrase.
lessons.pattern: G A B; B(1) A(1) G(2); written G-major fragment
quiz: B is which degree above G?

lessons.title: Hold half notes evenly
lessons.goal: Keep two-beat tones steady through a four-beat bar.
steps: Play G4 for1-2, A4 for3-4 at40 BPM; use the tongue only at the new note.
Play B4 for all four beats next bar, then rest a bar.
Compare tone stability at the beginning and end; do not shorten the half note to make a late breath.
quiz: A half note in this4/4 pattern lasts...

lessons.title: Original melody: Hill Song
lessons.goal: Play a two-bar B-A-G melody with a planned breath.
steps: Written | G A B A | G(2) B(1) G(1) | uses only left-hand notes.
Tongue the first note of each bar, then try connected changes for the rest; keep the same durations.
Breathe after bar2 and repeat. Sing the contour before the second take and give the last G a settled release.
lessons.pattern: | G A B A | G(2) B G |; written quarters/half note
quiz: In the middle of every note
An added beat before each A

lessons.title: A slur is not a tie
lessons.goal: Distinguish connected pitch changes from one held repeated pitch.
steps: Slur G4-A4-B4 with one starting tongue; air continues while fingers change.
Tie B across two one-beat durations and do not tongue the second written B.
Write a slur over G-A-B and a tie over B-B on paper. Compare the number of attacks by listening.
lessons.pattern: Slurred G-A-B; one B held for two tied beats
quiz: The same pitch into one longer duration

lessons.title: Add C to the upper fragment
lessons.goal: Play G-A-B-C with a clean B-to-C change.
steps: Written C5 uses left middle finger only; B4 left index only. Move both fingers together so an unintended open C# does not speak.
Play G-A-B-C then back, with slow stable air.
Hear B-C as a semitone, unlike G-A or A-B whole tones. Isolate B-C-B if the crossing squeaks.
lessons.pattern: Written G4 A4 B4 C5 and back; B-C semitone

lessons.title: Two light attacks per beat
lessons.goal: Tongue even eighth notes without tightening the jaw.
steps: Count1&2&3&4& at40 BPM; use a light dah articulation on B4 twice per beat.
Keep air moving behind the tongue; do not restart breath pressure for every subdivision.
Alternate one bar tongued and one bar slurred G-A-B-A-G-A-B-C, maintaining timing rather than forcing speed.
lessons.pattern: Eight written eighth notes per bar; light tongue versus one slurred air stream
quiz: For repeated eighths the air should...
Remain steady behind light tongue releases

lessons.title: G-B is a major third
lessons.goal: Hear a major third as a melodic chord fragment.
steps: Play written G4-B4, naming root and third of G major.
Compare G-A to G-B by humming the concert sounds; the interval quality survives transposition.
Make G-B-A-G as four quarters and hear G as home. A sax outlines harmony one note at a time, not as a polyphonic chord.
lessons.pattern: G-B major third; phrase G B A G
quiz: Sax can outline a chord by...
Sounding a full piano triad normally

lessons.title: Original melody: City Call
lessons.goal: Play a short pop phrase with clear tongue/slur choices.
steps: Tongue each numbered beat in bar1; slur A-B-C at the start of bar2.
Plan the breath after bar2 and give two takes. The equal-note reference does not reproduce the written half-beat placements.
lessons.pattern: Bar1 four quarters; bar2 two eighths plus three quarters; written pitch
quiz: The first A-B pair in bar2 fills...

lessons.title: Introduce F, E and D gently
lessons.goal: Add right-hand fingers without excessive key pressure.
steps: From written G close right index for F4, add middle for E4, add ring for D4; all three left main keys remain closed.
Move silently G-F-E-D and back before adding a comfortable breath.
Play just two notes per breath initially. If low D will not speak, check reed/setup and steady air rather than biting or pressing harder.
lessons.pattern: Written G4 F4 E4 D4 and back; no octave key
quiz: All six main keys without octave key

lessons.title: A six-note C-major fragment
lessons.goal: Play D-E-F-G-A-B-C with clear semitone changes.
steps: Use written D4-E4-F4-G4-A4-B4-C5; name E-F and B-C as semitones.
Practise D-E-F and G-A-B-C separately, then connect with a single gentle starting articulation.
Descend, keeping fingers near keys, and sing a phrase resolving C. Pitch labels show sharps only when an accidental is needed.
lessons.pattern: D E F G A B C; written notes, one quarter each

lessons.title: Breath marks belong to the phrase
lessons.goal: Place a breath after a complete two-bar idea.
steps: Write | E F G A | G(2) E(1) D(1) | followed by a breath mark.
Clap the durations, then finger silently while counting before playing.
Breathe after the phrase rather than interrupting a long note. Add a written rest if your comfortable breath needs more space.
lessons.pattern: | E F G A | G(2) E D |; breath after bar2
quiz: If a phrase exceeds comfortable breath, first...
Slowly practise or add a planned rest with musical intent
Bite the reed to save air

lessons.title: A three-beat melodic sway
lessons.goal: Keep three quarter beats in a3/4 phrase.
steps: Count1-2-3 with a light first-beat emphasis.
Play G4-A4-B4, then C5 for two beats and G4 for one.
Repeat, breathing after four bars; use your own three-beat count since the app's backing is four-beat.

lessons.title: Original melody: Meadow Song
lessons.goal: Create a measured answer to a lower-register phrase.
steps: Given written phrase | D E F G | A G E D | as quarters.
Write two answer bars using D-E-F-G-A-B-C, ending C5 for two beats with two beats silence.
Play all four bars with a planned breath after bar2. Assess relaxed air, right-hand movement and the exact final rest.
lessons.pattern: Two given4/4 bars; two original answer bars; final C(2),rest(2)
quiz: Durations for both notes and rests
Only the maximum number of pitches

lessons.title: Low C and C# key choices
lessons.goal: Sound low written C without forcing the reed.
steps: Low C4 closes all six main keys plus right little-finger low-C; low C#4 keeps those keys and adds left little-finger low-C#.
Finger D4-C4-D4 silently, keeping wrists comfortable while reaching pinkie keys.
Play two-beat tones with steady supported air and an open comfortable throat. Check leaks/setup with a teacher if low notes remain unreliable; never force volume.
lessons.pattern: Written D4 C4 C#4 D4; no octave key; two beats each

lessons.title: Written C major octave
lessons.goal: Play low C through middle C with no altered notes.
steps: Use C4-D4-E4-F4-G4-A4-B4-C5, checking low-C pinkie release into D.
Ascend one quarter per note then descend, breaking after four notes if needed.
Name E-F and B-C semitones; compare low and middle C tone without demanding equal loudness from the different registers.
lessons.pattern: Written C4 D4 E4 F4 G4 A4 B4 C5
quiz: Written C major's key signature has...

lessons.title: Bis Bb and written flats
lessons.goal: Use the bis Bb key and distinguish Bb from B.
steps: Written Bb4 can use left index on B plus the small bis key beneath it; the schematic labels this extra key.
Play A4-Bb4-C5 and back, avoiding accidental B natural.
Write the flat explicitly. The pitch guide displays A# for the same equal-tempered target, while the musical key spelling remains Bb.
lessons.pattern: A Bb C Bb A; bis Bb fingering; display may say A#
quiz: In this equal-tempered reference, Bb is the same pitch as...

lessons.title: F major with one flat
lessons.goal: Outline F major and name its triad.
steps: Play written F4-G4-A4-Bb4-C5-D5-E5-F5; for upper D,E,F use the octave key with their lower-stack main shapes.
If the upper register is not ready, practise F-G-A-Bb-C first and finish F below.
Outline F-A-C and hear root-third-fifth. The next unit develops register crossing; keep this first pass slow and comfortable.
lessons.pattern: F-major fragment F G A Bb C; triad F A C; optional upper-octave continuation

lessons.title: Original melody: Low River
lessons.goal: Shape a lower phrase with low-C release and clear Bb.
steps: Learn each two-bar breath group slowly, checking low-C pinkie timing and bis Bb.
Perform twice with a gentle rise to C5 and a quiet low-C ending. Pitch hits do not measure timbre or breath support.
lessons.pattern: Four4/4 bars in written F/C vocabulary; halves and quarters above
quiz: The Bb key should be used instead of...
B natural in this written phrase
The octave key on every note

lessons.title: Same fingers, lighter register change
lessons.goal: Move G4-G5 without biting the upper note.
steps: G4 uses left three main keys; G5 adds the thumb octave key with the same main fingering.
Play lower G then upper G with a comfortable continuous air stream; release into a breath rather than squeezing at the end.
Try both tongued and slurred octaves. If upper pitch is sharp, restore relaxed embouchure and ask a teacher about voicing instead of manipulating the reed harshly.
lessons.pattern: Written G4(2) G5(2), rest(4); octave-key contrast
quiz: G5 differs from G4 fingering by...

lessons.title: C#5 to D5 at the break
lessons.goal: Coordinate the large fingering change across the register break.
steps: Middle C#5 opens all six main keys with no octave; D5 closes all six and adds octave.
Move the fingers silently together before sounding C#-D.
Play B4-C#5-D5-E5 and reverse slowly, treating the break as a planned movement rather than a fast squeeze.
lessons.pattern: Written B4 C#5 D5 E5 D5 C#5 B4; coordinate octave thumb and main keys
quiz: All six main keys plus octave
All main keys open, no octave

lessons.title: Written D major, two sharps
lessons.goal: Play D major with F# and C# across the break.
steps: D4-E4-F#4-G4-A4-B4-C#5-D5; F#4 uses right middle rather than right index in the lower stack.
Practise C#5-D5-E5 separately, then reconnect with a measured breath after the phrase.
Descend, applying both sharps consistently. Sing C#-D to hear the leading tone resolve.
lessons.pattern: Written D major D E F# G A B C# D

lessons.title: Legato across different durations
lessons.goal: Slur a register change without altering note lengths.
steps: Play G4 for two beats and G5 for two; then A4 for one,B4 for one,D5 for two.
Clap durations first and finger silently while counting.
Use one starting tongue per bar, steady air through the break, and a measured rest after two bars. Timing remains self-assessed.
quiz: A new beat at the octave key

lessons.title: Original melody: High Bridge
lessons.goal: Connect lower and upper phrases with planned breath.
steps: Tongue phrase starts and slur each bar, then compare a gently tongued version.
Breathe after bar2, keep C# correct in bar3, and give two uninterrupted takes with a quieter final D.
lessons.pattern: Four4/4 bars in written D; final D5 whole note; breath after2
quiz: The written C in bar3 is...

lessons.title: Written A major, three sharps
lessons.goal: Play A major with C#, F# and G#.
steps: Use A4-B4-C#5-D5-E5-F#5-G#5-A5, adding octave from D5 upward.
G# uses the left little-finger G# key with the G main shape; keep that finger light.
Practise upper E-F#-G#-A separately, then play the full octave with an easy breath. Do not increase tempo while the break remains noisy.
lessons.pattern: Written A B C# D E F# G# A; one octave

lessons.title: Read the band's concert key
lessons.goal: Convert concert C major to written A major for alto.
steps: Alto written pitch is nine semitones above its sounding pitch, a major sixth; concert C4 becomes written A4.
Concert C-major harmony becomes written A major, including its three-sharp key signature.
Write concert C-D-E-G as written A-B-C#-E, then play the written notes and verify the tuner shows concert names. Do not also transpose the already-transposed app targets.
lessons.pattern: Concert C D E G -> written A B C# E; app handles sound transposition
quiz: Concert C major is written as which alto key?

lessons.title: Hear the written pop harmony
lessons.goal: Outline A-E-F#m-D for a concert C pop progression.
steps: Written triads A-C#-E, E-G#-B, F#-A-C#, D-F#-A correspond to concert C-G-Am-F.
Play the three tones as a melody, not a chord; name the minor third in F#m.
Land on the first tone of each new bar, then choose one upper chord tone on3. Hear chord quality even with a sparse line.
lessons.pattern: Written A-E-F#m-D; concert C-G-Am-F; melodic arpeggios

lessons.title: Dotted rhythm with air continuity
lessons.goal: Place an eighth after a dotted quarter accurately.
steps: Count1&2&3&4&; hold A4 from1 through2, play B4 on2&, C#5 on3 and E5 on4.
Tongue the new note lightly without restarting air pressure.
Repeat over written A-D-E-A roots in imagination or with a helper; clap the dotted rhythm before adding pitches.

lessons.title: Original melody: Neon Song
lessons.goal: Perform a transposed pop melody with accurate chord-tone landings.
steps: Harmony is written A-E-F#m-D, sounding concert C-G-Am-F; the app's concert C-F-G-C backing is not this exact progression.
Practise with the click or matching accompaniment, breathe after2, and give two takes with clean upper F#.
lessons.pattern: Four4/4 bars; written A-E-F#m-D harmony; half/quarter notes
quiz: The written harmony sounds in concert as...

lessons.title: Long-short eighths
lessons.goal: Use a triplet swing model while retaining quarter pulse.
steps: Count1-trip-let and play on1 and let; repeat four pairs on written G4.
Tongue lightly on the first of each pair and try slurring into the second, comparing articulations.
Alternate a straight-eighth bar with swing. The triplet ratio is a practice model; real swing changes with tempo and style.
lessons.pattern: Four long-short pairs per bar; first and third triplet slots

lessons.title: Written G-minor blues
lessons.goal: Play G-Bb-C-Db-D-F-G with a controlled passing tone.
steps: Name G4-Bb4-C5-Db5-D5-F5-G5; Db sounds the same as displayed C#.
Isolate C-Db-D across the register break, keeping fingers and octave thumb coordinated.
Create a two-beat phrase resolving G or D. The Db is a tension/passing colour, not necessarily the best long ending.
lessons.pattern: Written G Bb C Db D F G; blues scale
quiz: The passing tone between C and D is...

lessons.title: Written twelve-bar blues form
lessons.goal: Track a written G blues by bar number.
steps: Write G7 for1-4,C7 for5-6,G7 for7-8,D7 for9,C7 for10,G7 for11,D7 for12.
Play one written root per bar, then add root-third-seventh: G-B-F, C-E-Bb,D-F#-C.
Use a helper or metronome for this form; the app's generic concert backing is a different progression. Say bar numbers during the first pass.
lessons.pattern: 12 written bars G7 G7 G7 G7 C7 C7 G7 G7 D7 C7 G7 D7

lessons.title: Blues third versus chord third
lessons.goal: Compare Bb blues colour with B over G7.
steps: Written G7 contains G-B-D-F, but G-minor blues vocabulary includes Bb.
Play G-B-G-Bb and sing the colour difference in the concert sound.
Use Bb briefly in a call, then B as an answer landing over G7. Choose the contrast deliberately rather than playing an out-of-tune B.
lessons.pattern: G-B major chord third; Bb blues colour; intentional answer to call

lessons.title: Original melody: Blue Door
lessons.goal: Create a blues call and response with a planned rest.
steps: Call written G-Bb-C-D as eighths on1&2&, then rest3-4.
Answer B-D-F-D as the same rhythm over G7; repeat and vary only the last note.
Place the phrases in the twelve-bar form, choosing chord-tone endings at C7 and D7 changes. Write the response before improvising it.
lessons.pattern: Two-beat calls plus two beats rest, inside written twelve-bar G blues
quiz: A two-beat call followed by two beats rest fills...

lessons.title: Low B and Bb with patient air
lessons.goal: Explore low written B and Bb without forcing tone.
steps: Low B3 uses all six main keys, right low-C pinkie and left low-B pinkie; Bb3 changes the left pinkie to low-Bb while keeping main keys and right low-C closed.
Finger C4-B3-Bb3-B3-C4 silently, checking key reach with a teacher if uncomfortable.
Play short comfortable tones separated by full breaths. If low notes fail repeatedly, check instrument leaks/reed with a teacher instead of biting or blasting.
lessons.pattern: Written C4 B3 Bb3 B3 C4; no octave key; relaxed low-key table movement
quiz: Low written Bb adds to low-C fingering...

lessons.title: Palm D and Eb, a guided introduction
lessons.goal: Read and finger high D6 and Eb6 with a safe palm-key reach.
steps: Written high C6 uses middle C fingering plus octave; high D6 uses octave and left palm D with main keys open.
High Eb6 adds left palm Eb to palm D; the chart names these extra keys.
Finger silently first, then play C6-D6-Eb6-D6-C6 softly with rest between attempts. Teacher guidance is recommended; stop for strain and do not pursue altissimo here.
lessons.pattern: Written high C6-D6-Eb6-D6-C6; palm keys, no forced volume
quiz: Octave and palm D with main keys open

lessons.title: Written Bb major
lessons.goal: Apply Bb and Eb consistently in a Bb-major octave.
steps: Use Bb4-C5-D5-Eb5-F5-G5-A5-Bb5; Eb5 adds right little-finger Eb with upper D fingering and octave.
Check Bb choice and D-Eb separately before joining the scale.
Write the two-flat signature and play descending; distinguish scale spelling Eb from the guide's D# label.
lessons.pattern: Written Bb C D Eb F G A Bb; two-flat signature

lessons.title: Enclose a chord tone
lessons.goal: Resolve two neighbouring approach notes into a target.
steps: Target written E5 over C major; approach with F5 then D#5 then E5.
Count two eighth approaches on4 and4&, resolving E on next1.
Compare a diatonic D-E approach with this chromatic enclosure; write the D# explicitly and choose the target from the current chord.
lessons.pattern: F5-D#5 eighths on4,4& -> E5 next1; compare D-E

lessons.title: Original study: Chromatic Lane
lessons.goal: Perform chromatic approaches while keeping clear phrase destinations.
steps: Name every accidental; use G# pinkie and the C#-D break carefully.
Play twice with a planned breath after2. Hear C as the last phrase's home rather than interpreting the entire study as one scale.
lessons.pattern: Four written4/4 bars; chromatic approaches; final C5 whole note
quiz: Chromatic notes here should be heard as...
A reason to ignore the phrase
Automatic changes of key on every note

lessons.title: Three seventh-chord qualities
lessons.goal: Distinguish Cmaj7, Dm7 and G7 melodically.
steps: Written Cmaj7 C5-E5-G5-B5; Dm7 D5-F5-A5-C6; G7 G4-B4-D5-F5.
Play as quarter-note arpeggios and sing the sevenths; Cmaj7 B differs from C7 Bb.
Rest between patterns and simplify to thirds/sevenths if breathing becomes tight. No polyphonic sax chord is required.
lessons.pattern: Written Cmaj7, Dm7, G7 arpeggios; four quarters per chord

lessons.title: ii-V-I resolution
lessons.goal: Hear F resolve to E through a written G7-Cmaj7 cadence.
steps: Play written Dm7 F5-C6, G7 F5-B5, Cmaj7 E5-B5 as melodic pairs.
Sing concert versions and hear C fall to B then F fall to E; interval relationships stay unchanged by alto transposition.
Make a four-bar phrase anchored on those guide tones, with breath after2. Use pitch feedback for targets and listening for resolution.
lessons.pattern: Written ii-V-I guide tones F-C, F-B, E-B

lessons.title: D Dorian's natural sixth
lessons.goal: Use D Dorian around Dm7 chord tones.
steps: Written D5-E5-F5-G5-A5-B5-C6-D6 includes natural B, unlike D natural minor's Bb.
Practise the lower seven tones first; high D palm key is optional and can be replaced by returning to D5.
Use D-F-A-C as anchors and B as a brief colour. Sing before playing so the scale serves a phrase, not a mechanical run.
lessons.pattern: Written D Dorian fragment D E F G A B C then lower D; optional high palm D6

lessons.title: The band's ii-V-I in concert C
lessons.goal: Convert concert Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 to written Bm7-E7-Amaj7.
steps: Raise concert note names by a major sixth: D becomes B, G becomes E and C becomes A.
Written Bm7 B-D-F#-A; E7 E-G#-B-D; Amaj7 A-C#-E-G#.
Write all thirds and sevenths, then verify the app's written targets sound the concert chord tones. Do not transpose them a second time.
lessons.pattern: Concert Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 -> written Bm7-E7-Amaj7

lessons.title: Original melody: Cafe Air
lessons.goal: Perform a concert-C ii-V-I using the correct written alto notes.
steps: Written melody | D5(2) F#5(2) | G#4(1) F#4(1) D5(2) | C#5(2) B4(1) A4(1) | A4(4) | over Bm7-E7-Amaj7-Amaj7.
This sounds in concert Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Cmaj7; practise with a helper or metronome, not the generic backing.
Play two takes, breathing after2, then vary the first two durations while keeping a complete four-beat bar.
lessons.pattern: Written Bm7-E7-Amaj7-Amaj7; original ii-V-I melody; halves/quarters
quiz: The written final A harmony sounds...

lessons.title: Crescendo without pitch drift
lessons.goal: Shape a sustained tone while listening for tuning stability.
steps: Hold written G4 for four counts, growing from soft to moderate then easing back; rest at least four counts.
Use steady supportive air and comfortable embouchure; do not obtain volume by biting the reed.
Watch concert pitch on the tuner while listening to tone quality. If dizzy or strained, shorten the note and stop for normal breathing.
lessons.pattern: G4(4) with soft-moderate-soft arc; rest(4); repeat
quiz: Controlled volume with stable pitch and comfortable air

lessons.title: Optional upper palm E and F
lessons.goal: Read high E6 and F6 with instrument-specific key guidance.
steps: High E6 commonly uses octave, palm D/Eb and right-hand high-E side key; high F6 keeps those keys and adds left palm F.
Check key placement with a teacher, finger silently first, and keep main keys open as described in the chart.

Play D6-E6-F6-E6-D6 briefly and softly, resting between tries. If uncomfortable, read/finger the upper pattern silently and play D5-E5-F5-E5-D5 one octave lower for the practical take; altissimo is outside this course.
lessons.pattern: Written high D6 E6 F6 E6 D6; optional guided palm-key extension, lower-octave playing alternative
quiz: Use teacher-checked fingerings and stop for strain
Force volume until the note speaks

lessons.title: A harmonic minor in written pitch
lessons.goal: Play A harmonic minor and hear G# leading to A.
steps: Written A4-B4-C5-D5-E5-F5-G#5-A5 raises G from natural minor.
Practise F-G#-A slowly with coordinated pinkie movement; hear its wide step then semitone.
Outline E-G#-B then A-C-E as a minor cadence. Use the raised seventh deliberately rather than alternating G and G# randomly.
lessons.pattern: Written A B C D E F G# A; E-major -> A-minor cadence

lessons.title: Phrase accents without harsh attacks
lessons.goal: Emphasise a phrase high point without shortening neighbouring notes.
steps: Play written A4-C5-E5-C5 as quarters, giving E slightly more air intensity.
Repeat with E softer and the last A held two beats in a second bar; compare phrase direction.
Avoid tongue slaps or a jaw clamp to make accents. Keep the metronome pulse unchanged and choose the high point intentionally.
lessons.pattern: | A C E C | B(2) A(2) |; dynamic emphasis at E, not extra time
quiz: An accent should not accidentally change...

lessons.title: Original melody: Dusk Line
lessons.goal: Shape a minor melody with a controlled dynamic arc.
steps: Breathe after2, make F5 the phrase high point, and settle the final A softly without pitch collapse.
Give two takes with different planned articulation: slurred first, lightly tongued second. Assess tone, tuning, durations and the G# resolution separately.
lessons.pattern: Four4/4 bars in written A minor; G# dominant colour; final A whole note
quiz: An automatic modulation to F major

lessons.title: Repeat, sequence and answer
lessons.goal: Develop a short motif while retaining its rhythmic identity.
steps: Written motif A4-B4-C#5-rest as four quarter events; repeat once.
Sequence to D5-E5-F#5-rest, then answer C#5-B4-A4-rest.
Write a contrasting long-note version and perform both. Leave deliberate breathing space rather than filling every subdivision.
lessons.pattern: A B C# rest; D E F# rest; C# B A rest; written motif sequence
quiz: A recognisable motif variation can keep...

lessons.title: Pentatonic in the band's key
lessons.goal: Use written A-major pentatonic for concert C accompaniment.
steps: Written A-B-C#-E-F# sounds concert C-D-E-G-A.
Play slowly, then create a two-beat idea anchored on written A or C# over concert C.
Over concert F, aim for written F# or A; over concert G, aim E or B. Say written targets and their concert destinations before improvising.
lessons.pattern: Written A B C# E F# over concert C/F/G; chord-tone landings
quiz: Over concert F, written A sounds which chord tone?

lessons.title: Write a twelve-bar band roadmap
lessons.goal: Follow a transposed A-B-A form without double transposition.
steps: Concert A section is C-G-Am-F; concert B is Dm-G-C-C; perform A-B-A.
Write alto harmony A-E-F#m-D and Bm-E-A-A, numbering all twelve bars.
Play written roots first while a helper supplies concert chords. Confirm the app already converts written target audio down nine semitones.
lessons.pattern: Written12-bar A-B-A: A(A E F#m D), B(Bm E A A), A
quiz: The app's written alto targets should be...
Played as written, not transposed again
Lowered nine semitones by the player too

lessons.title: Prepare entries, fills and silence
lessons.goal: Choose chord-tone entries and leave room for other players.
steps: Over written A-E-F#m-D, choose C#-B-A-F# as the first melody note of each bar.
Write one rest before an entry and one two-beat answer at the end of a section, counting both explicitly.
Rehearse with a helper or matching backing, agreeing on concert key, count-in and final release. The microphone assesses single-pitch accuracy, not ensemble balance or style.
lessons.pattern: Written chord-tone entries C# overA, B overE, A overF#m, F# overD
quiz: Concert key, form, count-in and agreed ending
Only the loudest possible sax tone

lessons.title: Original melody: Open Horizon
lessons.goal: Perform a transposed A-B-A arrangement with a personal melodic return.
steps: Written A melody | C#5 E5 F#5 E5 | B4 E5 G#5(2) | A4 C#5 F#5 E5 | D5(2) C#5(1) A4(1) |; B melody | D5 F#5 A5 F#5 | G#4 B4 D5 B4 | C#5 E5 C#5 B4 | A4(4) |.
Use the previous twelve-bar written harmony roadmap, which sounds in concert C; breathe at two-bar boundaries or add a measured rest when needed.

Perform A-B-A with a motif variation in the final A, a planned dynamic contrast in B, and an agreed ending. Give two complete takes, assessing tone, transposition, rhythm, form and intentional phrasing.
